title: An etale stack with a representable diagonal and smooth atlas has fppf descent
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids on $S$-schemes: it has cartesian lifts along all base morphisms and groupoid fibres. Assume isomorphisms between objects form an etale sheaf and every etale descent datum for objects is effective. Suppose the diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], meaning that each sheaf $\operatorname{Isom}_T(a,b)$ for $a,b\in\mathcal X(T)$ is an algebraic space over $T$. Suppose there is an $S$-scheme $U$ and an object $x\in\mathcal X(U)$ such that the induced morphism $h_U\to\mathcal X$, with $h_U(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,U)$ as a discrete groupoid, is representable by algebraic spaces, smooth and surjective. This means that for every $T$ and $y\in\mathcal X(T)$, the space $W=h_U\times_{\mathcal X}h_T$ exists, $W\to T$ is smooth on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and its map on points is onto [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then isomorphisms in $\mathcal X$ form an fppf sheaf and every fppf descent datum for objects is effective [def-pc-fppf-site]. Thus $\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack, with the same representable diagonal and the same smooth surjective atlas $U$.

source.place: Tag 076V (lemma-stacks-etale), including its proof identifying the etale quotient presentation with its fppf quotient.

proof.text: Let $R=h_U\times_{\mathcal X}h_U$, the algebraic space supplied by the atlas hypothesis with $T=U$. Explicitly $R(T)$ consists of $(u,v,\alpha)$ with $u,v:T\to U$ and $\alpha:u^*x\cong v^*x$. Its two projections to $U$ are smooth: one is exactly the atlas base change with $T=U$, and the other is identified with it by $(u,v,\alpha)\mapsto(v,u,\alpha^{-1})$. Identity, inverse and composition are $(u,u,1)$, $(v,u,\alpha^{-1})$ and $(u,w,\beta\alpha)$. The groupoid laws hold because they are the laws for isomorphisms in $\mathcal X(T)$. Thus this is a smooth groupoid in algebraic spaces, with presheaf of groupoids $\mathcal P(T)=(U(T),R(T))$ and fully faithful functor $\mathcal P\to\mathcal X$ given by $u\mapsto u^*x$. These natural operations are morphisms of algebraic spaces by [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 04T4 (lemma-map-space-into-stack), explicit groupoid construction, as used for etale stacks in Tag 076V.

proof.text: Form $\mathcal E=a_{et}\mathcal P$ and extend $\mathcal P\to\mathcal X$ to $F:\mathcal E\to\mathcal X$ by [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description]. The map $F$ is fully faithful. Indeed, for objects of $\mathcal P$ its map on isomorphism sheaves is the sheafification of a bijection. For arbitrary $a,b\in\mathcal E(T)$ choose a common etale covering on which both come from $\mathcal P$, using the local-object assertion. On this covering and its pullbacks the map on isomorphisms is a bijection; unique gluing in the two isomorphism sheaves gives a bijection over $T$.

source.place: Tag 076V (lemma-stacks-etale), first quotient presentation paragraph; stacks.tex Tags 02ZP and 0436.

proof.text: For $y\in\mathcal X(T)$, its atlas pullback $W=h_T\times_{\mathcal X}h_U$ is smooth surjective over $T$ by assumption. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections] to obtain an etale covering $T_i\to T$ lifting to $W$. Such a lift is a map $u_i:T_i\to U$ and an isomorphism $u_i^*x\cong y|_{T_i}$. Hence $F$ is locally essentially surjective, so [lem-sfb-stack-fully-faithful-local-equivalence] gives $\mathcal E\simeq\mathcal X$.

source.place: Tag 076V (lemma-stacks-etale), claim and first equivalence; spaces-topologies.tex Tag 0CFV; stacks.tex Tag 046N.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-groupoid-fppf-quotient] to step 1 to form the fppf stack $\mathcal Q=a_{fppf}\mathcal P$; its atlas pullbacks are smooth surjective algebraic spaces. It is also an etale stack. In fact etale scheme maps are flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Thus every jointly surjective etale family is an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site], and the fppf sheaf and effective-descent conditions restrict to these families. The universal extension in [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description] gives $G:\mathcal E\to\mathcal Q$ extending $\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$.

source.place: Tag 076V (lemma-stacks-etale), second quotient paragraph; algebraic.tex Tag 04TK; topologies.tex Tag 021N (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf).

proof.text: The isomorphism presheaf between $u,v\in\mathcal P(T)$ equals $\operatorname{Isom}_T(u^*x,v^*x)$ by step 1. This is an algebraic space by the diagonal hypothesis, hence an fppf sheaf by [def-trf-algebraic-space], and also an etale sheaf by the covering inclusion in step 4. By [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description], its maps to the isomorphism sheaves in both $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal Q$ are bijections. Hence $G$ induces a bijection on these isomorphisms. Every pair of objects of $\mathcal E$ comes etale locally from $\mathcal P$; gluing in the isomorphism sheaves of the two etale stacks, exactly as in step 2, proves that $G$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Tag 076V (lemma-stacks-etale), full faithfulness of the comparison; spaces-groupoids.tex Tag 044V (lemma-quotient-stack-morphisms).

proof.text: For $q\in\mathcal Q(T)$ its atlas pullback is smooth surjective by [lem-sfb-smooth-groupoid-fppf-quotient]. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections] to it. The resulting lifts give objects $u_i\in U(T_i)$ and isomorphisms from their images to $q|_{T_i}$. Thus $G$ is etale locally essentially surjective. By [lem-sfb-stack-fully-faithful-local-equivalence], $G$ is an equivalence over the common category of schemes. Together with step 3 this identifies $\mathcal X$ with the fppf stack $\mathcal Q$.

Choose the pullback-compatible equivalence $H:\mathcal X\simeq\mathcal Q$ from steps 3 and 6, with inverse $K$ and unit $\eta:1\cong KH$. Full faithfulness identifies the two isomorphism presheaves, so the fppf sheaf condition transfers. Given an fppf descent datum $(x_i,\alpha_{ij})$ in $\mathcal X$, apply $H$ to its objects and arrows, using the pullback compatibilities. Its cocycle equations still hold. Effective descent in $\mathcal Q$ gives $q\in\mathcal Q(T)$ with compatible isomorphisms $q|_{T_i}\cong H(x_i)$. Applying $K$ and composing with $\eta_{x_i}^{-1}$ gives isomorphisms $d_i:K(q)|_{T_i}\cong x_i$. On each overlap, write the original transition as $\alpha_{ij}:x_i\to x_j$. The descended isomorphisms in $\mathcal Q$ satisfy $\beta_j=H(\alpha_{ij})\beta_i$. Applying $K$ and using naturality of $\eta$ gives $d_j=\alpha_{ij}d_i$, hence $d_jd_i^{-1}=\alpha_{ij}$, exactly the original datum. Thus the original datum is effective in $\mathcal X$. The diagonal and atlas conditions are unchanged scheme-test conditions, so the original $U$ is still a smooth surjective atlas.
